responsibilities: Build and own MPLC's analytics platform, creating trusted, governed data that supports reporting, decision-making and future AI capabilities.
Replace manual reporting processes with automated, reliable data products that give every part of the business confidence in the numbers they're using.
Some reporting processes are still manual today, and you'll be expected to challenge and improve them.
You'll spend as much time agreeing business definitions and understanding what metrics mean as you will writing SQL.
Reporting to the CIO, you'll own the analytics platform end-to-end, from data ingestion and modelling through to reporting, governance and data quality.

evidence.velocity_vs_rigour: Build and own MPLC's analytics platform, creating trusted, governed data
evidence.velocity_vs_rigour_explanation: The JD repeats trust, governance and data quality ("trusted, governed data", "same trusted source of truth") with no speed language.
evidence.domain_risk: ensuring content creators are paid fairly and organisations respect copyright
evidence.domain_risk_explanation: A licensing business where the role supports Finance and reporting, but the JD names no financial reporting, audit or regulatory exposure, so moderate.
evidence.data_team_maturity: You'll be MPLC's only Senior Analytics Engineer, so you'll need to be comfortable taking ownership and working independently.
evidence.data_team_maturity_explanation: A sole analytics engineer building "a modern data capability from the ground up", so the data function is early.
evidence.jd_authorship: You'll spend as much time agreeing business definitions and understanding what metrics mean as you will writing SQL.
evidence.jd_authorship_explanation: The candid "Let's be honest" section describes the actual day-to-day and current state, which reads as hiring-manager written.
evidence.stakeholder_orientation: Working closely with Revenue Operations, Finance and senior stakeholders
evidence.stakeholder_orientation_explanation: Revenue Operations (commercial) and Finance are named with equal weight as the primary audiences.
evidence.autonomy_level: you'll own the analytics platform end-to-end
evidence.autonomy_level_explanation: The role will "own the analytics platform end-to-end" and "help define the metrics that matter", which is strategic.
evidence.ai_role: creating trusted, governed data that supports reporting, decision-making and future AI capabilities
evidence.ai_role_explanation: The candidate builds the data foundation that future AI capabilities will consume, placing AI downstream of their work.
evidence.testing_framing: you'll own the analytics platform end-to-end, from data ingestion and modelling through to reporting, governance and data quality
evidence.testing_framing_explanation: Data quality is named as part of what the candidate owns, though no testing tool is listed.
evidence.loss_aversion_framing: give every part of the business confidence in the numbers they're using
evidence.loss_aversion_framing_explanation: Trust in the numbers dominates the role summary ("trusted numbers", "defined once, trusted by everyone"), reflecting fear of untrusted figures reaching the business.
evidence.greenfield_vs_fix: We're still building our technology foundations, so you'll be helping shape the future rather than stepping into a finished environment.
evidence.greenfield_vs_fix_explanation: The platform is being rebuilt "from the ground up", so the work is greenfield.
evidence.loss_aversion: Your goal is simple: make sure a number is defined once, trusted by everyone and never has to be rebuilt manually. — trust in a single source of truth is the central framing.
